summary.headline: SBFC Q1 FY27: PAT rose 29% YoY to INR 130 crores and spreads widened 39 bps QoQ to 9.48%, while 0+ DPD rose 70 bps and AUM grew 6% QoQ.
summary.overview: AUM reached INR 11,922 crores (up 27% YoY, 6% QoQ), with MSME AUM at INR 9,271 crores and gold loan AUM at INR 2,631 crores. Spreads improved to 9.48% and NIM to 10.6%, helped by a 90 bps YoY drop in cost of borrowing to 8.42%. Management cited headwinds: lower gold-loan eligibility after April 1, 2026 rules, a regulatory cap on bank collateral for sub-20 lakh MSME tickets that hit co-origination, and softer login-to-disbursal conversion (34% vs 42%). Asset quality weakened QoQ, with 0+ DPD up 70 bps and GNPA at 2.66%, but Stage 2 ECL was raised to 16% from 6% and total provisioning reached 1.91% of assets.

financial_highlights.change: up by similar bps as spread (QoQ)
Stage 2 ECL raised to 16% from 6%; about 2x regulatory minimum

segments.name: MSME / small-ticket LAP
segments.commentary: MSME AUM INR 9,271 crores (+4.5% QoQ) and disbursements INR 809 crores (+3% QoQ). Co-origination, about 20% of disbursals and book, reset to about 10% after RBI collateral rule for sub-20 lakh MSME tickets; management expects a return to usual run rate from this quarter.

segments.name: Gold loan
segments.commentary: AUM INR 2,631 crores (+11% QoQ). Gold yields rose in the quarter and were the main driver of the 29 bps QoQ yield increase; management expects gold yields to stay range-bound, with at most a marginal decline.

guidance_outlook: Opex to average AUM to fall 25 bps in FY27 (reiterated), and to be closer to 4% or below by year-end as new branches mature.
Credit cost expected at 1.4%-1.5% for at least the next two quarters; Q1 was 1.45%.
Yield expected to stabilise in the 17.50%-17.75% range; spreads to be held above 9%.
Cost of borrowing expected to stabilise at current levels after upfronting borrowings and liquidity build-up.
Branch expansion limited to 10-15 in FY27, after 5 branches added in Q1 (total 256), with further expansion tied to returns from recent branches.
Management says guidance for the coming quarter is unchanged; AUM target path to INR 15,000 crores with higher liquidity held on balance sheet.
capex_capacity: Branch count 256 as of June 2026 after adding five in Q1; roughly 52 branches opened over the last year, with the bulk in H2 FY26.
Plan for FY27 is 10-15 new branches, with expansion gated on profitability of recently opened branches.
Closing liquidity INR 1,864 crores; management intends to hold higher liquidity as it grows toward INR 15,000 crores AUM.
Capital adequacy ratio 32%; tangible net worth INR 3,613 crores.
demand_pricing: Login-to-disbursal conversion fell to 34% from 42%; management expects it to hold near 35% as higher logins and co-origination recover.
Around 1,400 applications per quarter (about 7% of roughly 21,000 logins), or about INR 140 crores of disbursals, were not passing filters; management will not push loans that fail screens.
Sub-10 lakh household segment showing leveraged stress; CIBIL scores above 700 for about 90% of the portfolio, but eligibility is the binding constraint.
Competitors pricing aggressively or offering larger loan amounts; management chose to walk away from some business to protect spreads.
Gold-loan eligibility norms reset from April 1, 2026, and falling gold prices reduced the loan amount reaching customers.

qa_highlights.question: Where is the sub-10 lakh segment in its credit cycle, and how does that affect FY27 growth and profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said conditions there have not improved and it is watchful. Aseem Dhru cited household DSR near 14% per CLSA, and said the company does not know whether it is early or mid-cycle.

qa_highlights.question: Will SBFC add new products in the next 12-18 months beyond small-ticket LAP and gold loans?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said it will focus on getting better at the existing two products and sees no need for new products or geographies to meet FY27 guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Increments were rolled out, and about 20-25 branches opened in Q4 FY26 plus 5 in Q1 brought their full-year staff costs into this quarter. Cost to AUM should fall as those branches mature over the next nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Was the 30 bps yield increase driven by higher risk-taking?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanket Agrawal said gold yields rose this quarter, adding to the yield improvement. Company yield is expected to stabilise at 17.50%-17.75%, with spreads held above 9%.

qa_highlights.question: Is credit cost stable at about 1.4% for the full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management expects credit cost of 1.4%-1.5% for at least the next two quarters; Q1 was 1.45%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for incremental yield and gold yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental yield is in the same 17.50%-17.75% range, slightly up because of gold. Gold yields are expected to be range-bound with at most a marginal fall; the recent 25-30 bps rise should not be extrapolated.

risks_watch: Sub-10 lakh household segment: management says conditions have not improved, CLSA household DSR near 14%, and the company cannot tell whether the cycle is early or mid; watch the disbursal mix and ticket size there.
Asset quality: 0+ DPD rose 70 bps QoQ and management called it homework for the current quarter, expecting stabilisation this quarter and rollbacks in later quarters; GNPA 2.66%.
Co-origination recovery: management expects co-origination to return to its usual run rate this quarter after the RBI collateral rule cut its share to about 10%; verify in Q2 disbursals.
Cost to AUM: opex 4.29% needs to fall to about 4% or below by year-end as branches opened in Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 mature; employee cost stays elevated in the near term.
Funding and rates: management flagged an upward bias in Indian interest rates from crude above $100 and deposit rates, while saying cost of borrowing should now stabilise at current levels.
Gold yields: management says the 25-30 bps rise should not be extrapolated and gold yields may drift marginally lower; spread floor of 9% depends on holding yields at 17.50%-17.75%.
key_quotes: We'd rather over-insulate the P&L now than explain a surprise later, call it prudence with a margin of safety.
So, we don't want to, at this stage look at anything different or new.
But I think the only parameter that one should probably look at is whether we've been able to maintain our spreads.
My sense is that the 25-30 basis increase you shouldn't pencil-in and extrapolate the numbers from here.
summary.management_tone: Confident on spreads, NIM, PAT and provisioning, with a cautious tone on the household segment and on macro, rates and oil. Management repeatedly stressed that guidance is unchanged and that it would rather slow growth than push loans that fail screens.

adds.what: 10-15 new branches in FY27 (256 branches as of June 2026 after 5 added in Q1)

growth.why: AUM grew 27% YoY to INR 11,922 crores and management targets INR 15,000 crores, but branch expansion is slowed to 10-15 in FY27 and login-to-disbursal fell to 34% from 42% with credit cost guided at 1.4-1.5%, so growth is positive but moderated.
